history.content: How does a bank make money on an interest free secured loan?
Generally, an interest-free loan will be tied to a specific purchase, so the banks make money from getting paid by the vendors of whatever was being purchased with the money that was lent.
The bank should be able to make money from the rate you are paying back for your unsecured line of credit.

original.scored_text:
You're right—my earlier explanation was misleading. A genuinely 0% loan does not generate interest payments while it remains interest-free.

According to page 1, many advertised 0% loans actually defer interest: if the borrower is late on a payment, all deferred interest becomes payable. Lenders count on some borrowers missing a payment.

Page 1 also explains that furniture or car financing can support profits from the item’s sale, so the loan itself need not earn money. Traditional banks and lenders would have to rely on fees if interest were not permitted. The document does not establish which arrangement applies to your particular loan.
